body.title: Specify one entry of the veto chain
body.body:
## What is delivered
A specification of one entry in the veto chain: its fields, what is signed, what is public and what is sealed.

Cover at least: the address of the contested decision; the grounds (intention, motives, scope, facts) and which parts can be sealed so that only triage reads them; how the entry proves that its signer is a member with standing in the affected context without revealing who they are; the hash of the previous entry; and the signature. Close with three worked entries in sequence: a veto, the triage outcome that answers it, and a panel order.

## Why it is needed
The veto chain is described in prose in this repository, and several others point to it: Dk, Dk Personal, Dk Network, the councils and the Drayker governance. Until an entry has a concrete shape, none of them can be designed against it, and the promise that a veto cannot be lost, forged or quietly ignored cannot be checked.

## Where to start
The section "The veto chain" in this repository's README. Existing append-only logs, certificate-transparency logs and anonymous-credential schemes are good prior art; say what each would get wrong here.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/#org/fn

body.title: Tie ratification to the constitutional procedure
body.body:
## What changed

- README and docs: Dk Global can append a proposal, never a ratification, and each change follows the constitutional procedure, built with Dk Global and within the kernel.
- llms.txt: Drayker is the supersystem.

## Founder

> "As mudanças na constituição sempre devem partir de um projeto super bem informado e validado feito em conjunto com o Dk global em cooperação com praticamente todos os membros de maior nível."

> "O Dk global deve apresentar uma alternativa ou uma aprovação da proposta, mas mudanças na constituição devem estar de acordo com o kernel, se não tiverem ele barra até que o kernel mude."

> "Isso apenas para constituição, certo? que já está ganhando destaque mais que suficiente, no resto o Dk global decide e executa autonomamente."

> "Com os membros podendo fazer o veto bem justificado."

> "Ela não é definível, a única definição que cabe é de super sistema."

body.title: Financing the network earns the reward
body.body:
The reward, the one transferable kind of reputation, is earned by contributing capacity such as computing **or by financing the network**. It gives faster or priority access to resources and never weighs in the members' constitutional choices. The reputation of work still cannot be purchased or transferred.

Removes the sentence saying the current proposal excludes financial contribution from reputation. README, docs and component contract are aligned.

Founder decision (06/10/2026): "quem financia também ganha essa mesma reputação".

body.title: uid: personhood rests on multi-factor biometrics
body.body:
## What changes
- **README and docs/README:** a paragraph on personhood. Only a UID holder can access the system, and each UID corresponds to one living person. Personhood is established by multi-factor biometrics, certified by people at enrolment and verified continuously, which makes fake or duplicated members close to impossible and keeps coordinated crowds of fake accounts out of the network's debates. The data belongs to the member, who sees what is collected and why; it is not kept in a central database; anonymity towards other members remains possible, as with the justified veto.
- **The PAP paragraph** now says personhood verification belongs to UID instead of leaving it open.
- **component.yml:** biometric personhood enters the scope. The non-scope keeps "a central biometric database" instead of any biometric database. A new risk names biometric data used beyond what the member can see and has agreed to.

## Why
This is the founder's design for UID. Edits in August and September moved biometrics out of scope ("no biometric database") without that decision being his.

body.title: A contested triage goes to a member council
body.body_html:
Aligns this repository with the decisions of October 2026:

  • member councils formed for each question instead of an independent judicial panel chosen by lot;
  • no forks or open-code claims for Dk: auditable through Dknowledge and DFM by permission level, with divergence tested in parallel;
  • Dk Global decides only inside the space the constitution gives it, open to representation, proposals and justified vetoes;
  • units of account instead of a token economy.

body.title: Specify the veto chain: grounds, weighing, advanced triage
body.body:
Alignment pass across the `draykerdk` organization, on the branch `alinhamento/2026-09` in every affected repository.

## Changes

- docs: specify the veto chain
- docs: vetoes carry their grounds; weighing and advanced triage
- docs: remove book citations

## Across the organization

- Governance corrected: PAP is Projects & Applications, DFMP is the DFM proposal process, the founding account is `Hyadhuad`, and the governance horizon runs from the founding Embassy through the DAF into PAP.
- The veto chain specified in UID: signed, hash-linked vetoes that carry their real grounds even when anonymous; vetoes weighed by grounds, not counted; one veto with grounds beyond the decision's scope can lead to an adjustment after advanced triage.
- Direction states 2033 as the objective, measured by what works rather than by the date.
- Intelligence is a partner, never the master.
- English is the canonical documentation language.
- Documentation states its own claims and does not cite outside books as authority.

Documentation only. Nothing here claims an implemented system.

Supersedes #3, closed when the branch was renamed.

body.title: Write the identity requirements
body.body:
## What is delivered
A requirements document for UID: what a universal identity in this ecosystem must guarantee, and what it must never do.

Cover at least: what an identity is bound to; how a participant proves control of one; whether identities can be separated or held pseudonymously; how contribution history attaches to an identity; and what happens when an identity is lost.

## Why it is needed
UID is described as the primary system design and the basis for every application on the platform. No requirements are published, so nothing about it can be designed against or argued with from outside.

For a system whose premise is that strangers cooperate, how identity works is not a detail to postpone.

## Where to start
Prior art and objections are as welcome here as proposals. What existing identity systems get wrong is a good place to begin.
## Prior material

Drayker has earlier work on this subject in its own knowledge base — drafts, mostly in Portuguese, written before the public repositories took their current shape. It is not published yet. If you take this function, say so in the thread and the relevant material will be published alongside it, so you are consolidating and arguing with existing thinking rather than starting from a blank page.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest.
